title: Working at Redwood: roles, career ladders, benefits, hiring & onboarding, and internal tools
author: Sofia Patel
body:
Overview

This document describes what it means to work at Redwood, the structure of our role and career ladders, the benefits and perks we provide, a high-level hiring and onboarding overview, and the primary internal tools new employees will use. It is intended as a single, practical reference for candidates, new hires, hiring managers, and people-ops partners.

Contents
1) Working at Redwood — culture & expectations
2) Roles & career ladders (IC + manager paths)
3) Benefits and perks (summary & eligibility)
4) Hiring process (standard interview loop and offer flow)
5) New hire onboarding (preboarding, first week, 30/60/90)
6) Internal tools (access, owners, quick tips)

---

1) Working at Redwood — culture & expectations
Intro: Redwood is an engineering-first company focused on building a production-grade inference platform. We value ownership, clear communication, operational rigor, and continuous learning. All employees are expected to: act with customer empathy, ship with quality, collaborate across teams, and communicate decisions and tradeoffs clearly.

Core principles
- Customer-first production mindset: shipping reliable, observable services matters as much as model improvements.
- Ownership and clarity: document decisions, name owners, and create measurable outcomes.
- Iterative improvement: small, frequent experiments with clear metrics.
- Inclusive collaboration: diverse perspectives accelerate better systems.

Performance expectations
- Use quarterly goals and 1:1s to align on priorities.
- Provide timely status updates for cross-team dependencies via the team roadmap and Slack channels.
- Follow security and compliance guidance (see security-and-compliance docs for required training).

---

2) Roles & career ladders (IC + manager paths)

Overview: Our career framework has two primary paths — Individual Contributor (IC) and Manager. Progression is level-based and includes clear expectations across four dimensions: impact, technical/product depth, leadership (influence and mentorship), and execution.

Role tiers (typical engineering example)
- IC1 (Associate Engineer): learning the codebase, shipping small features with supervision.
- IC2 (Engineer): owns small services/features end-to-end; reliable execution.
- IC3 (Senior Engineer): leads medium-sized projects and mentors peers; drives cross-team improvements.
- IC4 (Staff Engineer): defines architecture for multi-team systems, drives high-impact initiatives.
- IC5 (Principal/Distinguished): company-level technical leadership, long-term strategy, cross-company influence.
- Manager levels: Manager, Senior Manager, Director (engineering managers follow a similar progression focusing on people management, hiring, and organizational outcomes).

What we evaluate for promotion (summary)
- Impact: measurable improvements to customers, latency/cost reductions, or revenue enablement.
- Scope: breadth and complexity of problems owned.
- Leadership: influence beyond the team, mentoring, and cross-functional collaboration.
- Craft: code quality, architecture, and design decisions.
- Reliability & operability: SLO ownership, incident reduction, and runbook quality.

Promotion process (high-level)
1. Candidate (engineer or manager) and manager discuss readiness and submit a promotion packet (role summary, 2-3 signal projects, feedback).
2. Calibration panel (peer reviewers + manager) reviews packet against rubric.
3. Decision & communication within 14 business days of packet submission.
4. If promoted: update grade, compensation, and manager will create a 90-day success plan.

Career development resources
- Quarterly calibration cycles and leveling calibration docs (see related_pages).
- Learning stipend (see benefits) and mentorship program.
- Regular career conversations in 1:1s and annual career ladders workshops.

---

3) Benefits and perks (summary & eligibility)

Summary of primary benefits (US-focused summary — see regional benefits pages for local differences)
- Health & welfare: medical, dental, vision plans with employer contribution (standard plan: employer covers ~85% of employee premium; see benefits admin for details).
- Retirement: 401(k) with company match up to 4% of salary after first 90 days.
- Equity: standard RSU grant at hire, recurring annual refresh grants for most full-time roles.
- Time off: 20 days PTO (accrual-based) + 10 company holidays + flexible sick leave. Managers may approve extended unpaid leave on a case-by-case basis.
- Parental leave: 16 weeks primary caregiver, 8 weeks secondary caregiver (paid, in addition to disability where applicable).
- Stipends and allowances: $500 home office stipend at hire; $1,500 annual learning & development stipend.
- Wellness: monthly mental health stipend and access to EAP.
- Commuter: pre-tax commuter benefits where applicable.

Perks for remote & hybrid employees
- Home office budget and ergonomic equipment support.
- Regional coworking credits for teams that use office-adjacent hubs.

Eligibility & administration
- Benefits eligibility typically begins on the first day of employment for full-time employees; contractors receive reduced/limited benefits.
- People-ops manages enrollments via the HRIS (PeopleSoft/BambooHR link in internal tools). For questions: people-ops@redwood.com.

---

4) Hiring process (standard interview loop and offer flow)

High-level interview steps (typical for engineering roles)
1. Recruiter screen: role fit, compensation expectations, logistics.
2. Hiring manager screen: technical background and initial alignment.
3. Take-home assessment or technical exercise (used selectively).
4. Onsite / virtual loop (4 interviews): coding/design, system design, product sense/behavioral, and a meeting with hiring manager or cross-functional partner.
5. Debrief & calibration: interviewers submit feedback; hiring committee reviews for fit and compensation banding.
6. Offer: recruiter extends verbal + written offer and coordinates background check.

Standard timing targets
- Initial screen: within 3 business days of application or referral.
- Loop scheduling: target within 10 business days after phone screens.
- Offer decision: target within 5 business days of onsite loop completion.

Inclusive hiring guidance
- Use structured rubrics and job-specific evaluation criteria.
- Diverse interview panels where possible and inclusive interview training for interviewers.

Hiring manager checklist (short)
- Create/update role brief and a clear rubric.
- Assign interviewers and confirm rubric questions.
- Schedule calibration after interviews.
- Partner with recruiter for candidate experience and debrief timelines.

---

5) New hire onboarding (preboarding, first week, 30/60/90)

Preboarding (before day 1)
- Complete HR paperwork and benefits enrollment link sent by people-ops.
- IT will provision laptop, create Okta account, and invite to Slack and Confluence.
- Manager sends welcome note with Day 1 schedule and a short list of reading materials.
- New hire receives onboarding checklist in Confluence and a calendar invite for new hire orientation.

First week (day-by-day checklist)
| Day | Goals & tasks | Owners/Notes |
|-----|---------------|-------------|
| Day 1 | HR welcome, equipment handoff, Slack login, security training (basic), sign policies | people-ops, IT |
| Day 2 | Join team standup, access GitHub & Jira, set up dev environment, run local tests | Manager, buddy |
| Day 3 | Product overview, architecture walkthrough, first small task assigned | Tech lead |
| Day 4 | Meet cross-functional partners (SRE, product, support), read runbooks | Manager |
| Day 5 | Deliver first small PR or documentation update, 1:1 with manager to set 30-day goals | Manager, Buddy |

Buddy program
- Every new hire is assigned a buddy from the team for the first 90 days. The buddy helps with culture, codebase orientation, and small day-to-day questions.

30/60/90 plan (example)
- 30 days: complete essential training, ship first small change, understand codebase and deployment flow.
- 60 days: own a mid-sized task end-to-end, participate in oncall rotation training (if applicable).
- 90 days: take ownership of a feature area, present a short retrospective on onboarding and initial impact.

Onboarding completion & success metrics
- Manager and new hire review the 90-day plan and mark success criteria in Confluence. People-ops runs a 30/90-day check-in survey for continuous improvement.

---

6) Internal tools (access, owners, quick tips)

Primary tools and quick notes
- Slack (primary comms): channels include #all, #random, #eng-infra, #sre-oncall, and team channels. Use threads to keep channels readable. (owner: IT/Comms)
- Confluence (documentation): canonical source for runbooks, design docs, and this handbook. Use templates when creating new pages. (owner: people-ops)
- GitHub (code host): org name: redwood-inference. Team-based repo access via GitHub teams and Okta SSO. Follow our branching and PR templates. (owner: eng-platform)
- Jira (work tracking): project boards per org area. Create tasks with clear acceptance criteria and attach design docs. (owner: eng-platform)
- Okta / SSO & Identity: central login for all internal apps. MFA required. For access issues, contact IT. (owner: security-and-compliance)
- HRIS & payroll: BambooHR (or PeopleSoft depending on region). Use for time-off requests and benefits enrollment. (owner: people-ops)
- Redwood Console (internal): internal staging URL for deployment testing and service dashboards. Not for customer data unless explicitly authorized. (owner: eng-platform)
- Dev sandbox: dev.redwood.local for local integration tests and short-lived clusters. Use ephemeral credentials and follow sandbox usage policies. (owner: eng-infra)
- Monitoring & Alerts: Datadog for metrics & alerting; Sentry for error tracking. SLO dashboards live in the eng-platform dashboards folder. (owner: eng-sre)

Access request & onboarding support
- Standard access request: open an IT ticket at it-help@redwood.com including new hire name, role, required repos/tools, and manager approval.
- Escalations: for access needed urgently on Day 1, tag IT and people-ops in the access request.

Security & compliance reminders
- Complete security awareness training on Day 1.
- Enable MFA on Okta and follow password manager guidance.
- For customer-sensitive work or private deployment projects, follow additional data handling procedures in security-and-compliance.

---

Feedback and updates
This handbook page is maintained by People Ops. Send updates, suggestions, or broken links to people-ops@redwood.com. We run quarterly reviews of handbook content to keep role expectations, benefits, and tooling lists current.
